title: The Knight’s Return
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the knight underpromotion, queen-promotion stalemate, and king activation after winning the queen. The checking knight is offered indirectly: ...Kxc6 captures the original knight.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, black has an overwhelming material advantage, having a queen for a knight and a pawn. But in the great game of chess, you cannot write off any position without concrete calculation. So, white starts with B7 check, forcing the king to A7, and now gives another check with the knight. The black king has only two choices, either A6 or B6. But if he goes to B6, it is simple to see that white can simply promote to a queen with check, and even if the knight falls, there is going to be a simple sequence that wins the black queen and the game. But black is not that naive, and instead of allowing this sequence, he's simply going to play king to [music] A6, setting up a surprising trap. Because if white now promotes to a queen, this is actually a mistake because of the brilliant queen D7, sacrificing the last piece that black has. Since white has no other choice but to collect this queen and allow a stalemate and thus a draw. So, is this it? Is black simply out of the woods in this position? Well, not exactly. White has the brilliant and very rare under promotion to a knight, an incredible concept that keeps the game going since it's a check and forces the king to B6. But now surely there is no way for white to actually win this position. He's still down material having two knights for the queen. But you see, white has another brilliant idea and sacrifices one of the knights with knight to D7 check. If the knight is not taken, knight C5 is simply going to be a fork, picking up the queen and easily [music] winning the game. But if black decides to take the white knight right away, now there is going to be another fork, picking up the queen and seemingly winning the game. But black has not played his last card yet, and he can go king to C4, now attacking the knight and the pawn at the same time. If you try to save the knight, you're going to lose the pawn and this is still a draw because the knight cannot possibly checkmate. But just as black starts celebrating this draw, white plays king to c7. One last majestic sacrifice. Of course, the pawn cannot be taken. But if the knight is taken, now the king is going to attack the black pawn. And after black defends it, there is going to be king a5, effectively setting up a zugzwang. Because it is black to move and the only square from which black can defend the black pawn is exactly where the king is. So, after the king moves, white is going to collect the black pawn, promote his last pawn, and win this game. [music]
